# morar <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/viniciusoike/morar/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/viniciusoike/morar/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
<!-- badges: end -->

morar computes housing affordability for fixed-rate Brazilian mortgage
scenarios. It answers two questions: how much income a household needs to buy
a given property, and how expensive a property a given income and down payment
can support. It handles SAC, Price and mixed amortization, effective and
nominal rates, insurance (MIP and DFI) and administrative fees. Every core
function is vectorized, so it works on income or price distributions inside
`dplyr::mutate()`.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("viniciusoike/morar")
```

## Income and price

`min_income()` returns the monthly income needed to finance a property, and
`max_price()` inverts it. By default the first payment may take 30% of
income. The default loan-to-value ratio uses a Caixa SBPE convention checked
in September 2026; pass `ltv` for another product or lender.

```{r}
library(morar)

# Income needed for a R$ 500k property at 11% a.a., SAC, 80% LTV
min_income(500000, i = 0.11)

# Most expensive property each income can finance
max_price(c(5000, 10000, 20000), i = 0.11)
```

Pass `cash` to cap the price at what the available down payment supports. The
lower of the income and cash limits binds. `loan_summary()` reports the
required down payment for a property. The chosen `ltv` stays fixed; extra
cash does not reduce the modeled loan.

```{r}
max_price(10000, i = 0.11, ltv = 0.8)
max_price(10000, i = 0.11, ltv = 0.8, cash = 50000)
loan_summary(250000, i = 0.11, ltv = 0.8)$down_payment
```

The first payment includes insurance and fees. MIP depends on the borrower's
age, so charges default to zero; pass your own rates to include them.

```{r}
min_income(
  500000,
  i = 0.11,
  mip_rate = 0.0003,
  dfi_rate = 0.00008,
  admin_fee = 25
)
```

`loan_summary()` returns every component at once:

```{r}
loan_summary(c(300000, 500000, 800000), i = 0.11, method = "price")
```

## Amortization schedules

`amortization_table()` builds the month-by-month schedule for one loan.

```{r}
amortization_table(500000, i = 0.11, n = 420, admin_fee = 25)
```

## Affordability indices

The Housing Affordability Index (HAI) compares a household's income with the
qualifying income: 100 means it qualifies exactly. The price-to-income ratio
(PIR) divides the price by annual income and maps to the Demographia
categories.

```{r}
calc_hai(price = 400000, income = 8000, i = c(0.08, 0.11, 0.14))

pir <- calc_pir(price = 500000, income = 10000, annual_factor = 40 / 3)
pir
pir_category(pir)
```

## Conventions

- Rates are decimals: `0.11` means 11% a.a. The schedule uses a fixed monthly
  interest rate. It does not model TR or IPCA adjustment of the outstanding
  balance.
- `rate_type = "effective"` (default) compounds the annual rate;
  `"nominal"` divides it by 12.
- Affordability uses the first payment, the highest one under SAC. This is an
  estimate of qualifying income, not a bank approval decision.
- `ltv = NULL` uses `default_ltv(method)`: 80% for SAC, 70% for Price and
  mixed, under the dated Caixa SBPE convention above.
- `cash` covers the down payment only. Purchase taxes, registration and other
  upfront costs are outside the calculation.
- `calc_pir()` annualizes income with `annual_factor = 12`; use `40 / 3` to
  include the 13th salary and the vacation bonus.
